###merge all 20 tables together into one mega table for analysis

```{r}
BR5_taxonomy_ALL <- rbind(BR5_taxonomy_1, BR5_taxonomy_2, BR5_taxonomy_3, BR5_taxonomy_4, BR5_taxonomy_5, BR5_taxonomy_6, BR5_taxonomy_7, BR5_taxonomy_8, BR5_taxonomy_9, BR5_taxonomy_10, BR5_taxonomy_11, BR5_taxonomy_12, BR5_taxonomy_13, BR5_taxonomy_14, BR5_taxonomy_15, BR5_taxonomy_16, BR5_taxonomy_17, BR5_taxonomy_18, BR5_taxonomy_19, BR5_taxonomy_20)
```

###filter out all rows where kingdom = "no match"

```{r}
BR5_alltaxa_withmatch <- filter(BR5_taxonomy_ALL, Kingdom != "NoMatch") 
```

##How many sequences got reads to phylum? class? order? genus? species? 

```{r}
BR5phylum_count <- sum(!is.na(BR5_alltaxa_withmatch$Phylum))
BR5class_count <- sum(!is.na(BR5_alltaxa_withmatch$Class))
BR5order_count <- sum(!is.na(BR5_alltaxa_withmatch$Order))
BR5genus_count <- sum(!is.na(BR5_alltaxa_withmatch$Genus))
BR5species_count <- sum(!is.na(BR5_alltaxa_withmatch$Species))
```

##what are the dominant reads

```{r}
#remove all no match from at phylum level
br5_MATCH_phyla <- filter(BR5_alltaxa_withmatch, Phylum != "NoMatch")

#what are the dominant phyla?
BR5phylum_counts <- br5_MATCH_phyla %>%
  count(Phylum, sort = TRUE)

#what are the dominant class?
BR5class_counts <- br5_MATCH_phyla %>%
  count(Class, sort = TRUE)

#what are the dominant order?
BR5order_counts <- br5_MATCH_phyla %>%
  count(Order, sort = TRUE)

#what are the dominant genus?
BR5genus_counts <- br5_MATCH_phyla %>%
  count(Genus, sort = TRUE)

#what are the dominant species?
BR5species_counts <- br5_MATCH_phyla %>%
  count(Species, sort = TRUE)
```

##macroinvert phyla -> filter for aquatic invertebrates as published in thorp and covich 
```{r}
#remove all no match from at phylum level
br5_MATCH_phyla <- filter(BR5_alltaxa_withmatch, Phylum != "NoMatch")

#create df for each phyla published in thorp and covich
BR5_protozoa <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Protozoa")
BR5_porifera <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Porifera")
BR5_turbellaria <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Turbellaria")
BR5_nemertea <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Nemertea")
BR5_gastrotricha <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Gastrotricha")
BR5_rotifera <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Rotifera")
BR5_nematoda <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Nematoda")
BR5_nematomorpha <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Nematomorpha")
BR5_mollusca <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Mollusca")
BR5_annelida <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Annelida")
BR5_bryozoa <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Bryozoa")
BR5_tardigrada <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Tardigrada")
BR5_arthropoda <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Phylum == "Arthropoda")

#create one large dataframe with all of the phyla above
BR5_invert_phyla <- rbind(BR5_protozoa, BR5_porifera, BR5_turbellaria, BR5_nemertea, BR5_gastrotricha, BR5_rotifera, BR5_nematoda, BR5_nematomorpha, BR5_mollusca, BR5_annelida, BR5_bryozoa, BR5_tardigrada, BR5_arthropoda)

BR5_invertphylum_counts_ <- BR5_invert_phyla %>%
  count(Phylum, sort = TRUE)
```

##from the invert phyla, extract all species that are within phyla that have freshwater inverts

```{r}
invertBR5species <- BR5_invert_phyla %>% filter(!is.na(Species))

```


##macroinvert order

```{r}
BR5_coleoptera <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Order == "Coleoptera")
BR5_diptera <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Order == "Diptera")
BR5_ephemeroptera <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Order == "Ephemeroptera")
BR5_hemiptera <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Order == "Hemiptera")
BR5_plecoptera <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Order == "Plecoptera")
BR5_trichoptera <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Order == "Trichoptera")
BR5_Odonata <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Order == "Odonata")
BR5_Megaloptera <- filter(br5_MATCH_phyla, Order == "Megaloptera")
```

#Merge species into one DF to check for aquatic

```{r}
#merge all 3 species dataframes
invert_phyla_species_toCHECK <- rbind(invertBR5species, invertCOIF230species ,invertUNICOIspecies)

#get list of all species present with how many reads
invert_phyla_species_toCHECK_counts_ <- invert_phyla_species_toCHECK %>%
  count(Species, sort = TRUE)

taxonomyinvert_phyla_species_toCHECK_counts_ <- distinct(invert_phyla_species_toCHECK, Species, .keep_all = TRUE)

#just species as a csv
write.csv(invert_phyla_species_toCHECK_counts_,"proccessedData/tables/tables_toCheck/invert_phyla_species_toCHECK.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#whole taxonomy as a csv
write.csv(taxonomyinvert_phyla_species_toCHECK_counts_,"proccessedData/tables/tables_toCheck/taxonomyinvert_phyla_species_toCHECK_counts_.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

#filter for aquatic taxa
##fully aquatic insect taxa
```{r}

ephemeroptera_allprimerinverts <- filter(invert_phyla_species_toCHECK, Order == "Ephemeroptera")

plecoptera_allprimerinverts <- filter(invert_phyla_species_toCHECK, Order == "Plecoptera")
odonata_allprimerinverts <- filter(invert_phyla_species_toCHECK, Order == "Odonata")
megaloptera_allprimerinverts <- filter(invert_phyla_species_toCHECK, Order == "Megaloptera")

```

##check against chelsea's list of aquatic insect taxa ()
```{r}
#create dataframe for each order in chelsea's list

hemiptera_notcleaned <- filter(invert_phyla_species_toCHECK, Order == "Hemiptera")
```

```{r}
## Simple GBIF US occurrence checker
install.packages("rgbif")
library(rgbif)
library(dplyr)

# Load your species list (a CSV with one column called "species")
species_list <- read.csv("proccessedData/tables/tables_toCheck/species_tocheck_inGBIF.csv")$Species

# Check each species for US occurrences
results <- data.frame(species = character(), found_in_us = logical(), n_records = integer())

for (sp in species_list) {
  res <- occ_search(scientificName = sp, country = "US", limit = 1)
  n <- ifelse(is.null(res$meta$count), 0, res$meta$count)
  gbif_us_results <- rbind(results, data.frame(species = sp, found_in_us = n > 0, n_records = n))
  Sys.sleep(0.5)  # avoid hammering the API
}

# View and save results
print(gbif_us_results)
write.csv(results, "proccessedData/tables/database_search/gbif_us_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

##check species for aquatic using GBIF (code mostly from claude via penn state AI studio)
###THIS DIDNT WORK
###set up
```{r}
library(rgbif)

#load the species list
species_list <- read.csv("proccessedData/tables/database_search/GBIF_USspecies_foraquaticcheck.csv")$species

# Keywords considered "aquatic" - checked against habitat text GBIF returns
aquatic_keywords <- c("marine", "freshwater", "wetland", "aquatic", "river",
                       "lake", "stream", "coastal", "estuar", "ocean", "sea")

results <- data.frame(
  species = character(),
  aquatic = character(),   # "aquatic", "terrestrial", "unknown"
  habitats = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (sp in species_list) {

  # Step 1: resolve species name to a GBIF taxon key
  match <- tryCatch(name_backbone(name = sp), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (is.null(match) || is.null(match$usageKey)) {
    results <- rbind(results, data.frame(species = sp, aquatic = "unknown", habitats = NA))
    next
  }

  # Step 2: pull habitat data for that key (no API key required)
  hab <- tryCatch(name_usage(key = match$usageKey, data = "habitats"),
                  error = function(e) NULL)

  if (is.null(hab) || is.null(hab$data) || nrow(hab$data) == 0) {
    results <- rbind(results, data.frame(species = sp, aquatic = "unknown", habitats = NA))
  } else {
    habitat_text <- tolower(paste(hab$data$name, collapse = "; "))
    is_aquatic <- any(sapply(aquatic_keywords, function(k) grepl(k, habitat_text)))
    results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
      species = sp,
      aquatic = ifelse(is_aquatic, "aquatic", "terrestrial"),
      habitats = habitat_text
    ))
  }

  Sys.sleep(0.3)  # be polite to the API
}

print(results)
write.csv(results, "proccessedData/tables/database_search/aquatic_status_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Species with no habitat data - need manual check or a secondary source
unknowns <- filter(results, aquatic == "unknown")
print(unknowns)
```

##use WORMS (world registrar of marine species) to identify aquatic species and if they are freshwater or marine

```{r}
#load worms package
#install.packages("worrms")
library(worrms)

#load species list
species_list <- read.csv("proccessedData/tables/database_search/GBIF_USspecies_foraquaticcheck.csv")$species
 
results <- data.frame(
  species = character(),
  aquatic = character(),    # "aquatic", "terrestrial", "unknown"
  source  = character(),    # "WoRMS"
  detail  = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
 
for (sp in species_list) {
 
  status <- "unknown"
  source <- NA
  detail <- NA
 
  worms_hit <- tryCatch(wm_records_name(sp, marine_only = FALSE),
                         error = function(e) NULL)
 
  if (!is.null(worms_hit) && nrow(worms_hit) > 0) {
    rec <- worms_hit[1, ]
    flags <- c(rec$isMarine, rec$isBrackish, rec$isFreshwater)
    is_aquatic <- any(flags %in% 1, na.rm = TRUE)
    is_terrestrial_only <- isTRUE(rec$isTerrestrial == 1) && !is_aquatic
 
    if (is_aquatic) {
      status <- "aquatic"
    } else if (is_terrestrial_only) {
      status <- "terrestrial"
    }
 
    source <- "WoRMS"
    detail <- paste0("marine=", rec$isMarine, "; brackish=", rec$isBrackish,
                      "; freshwater=", rec$isFreshwater,
                      "; terrestrial=", rec$isTerrestrial)
  } else {
    source <- "none"
    detail <- "no WoRMS record found"
  }
 
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
    species = sp,
    aquatic = status,
    source  = source,
    detail  = detail,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))
 
  Sys.sleep(0.5)
}
 
write.csv(results, "proccessedData/tables/database_search/aquatic_status_results_worms.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

##since there are no ESVs that overlap as long as the esvs get a column with primer name for any downstream analysis/issues, the header on the pools can be removed and the ESVs can be merged into one large table

```{r}

#remove the prefix in columns 3-67 that keep the columns in each dataframe from lining up
names(raw_ESV_BR5)[3:67] <- sub("^BR5_", "", names(raw_ESV_BR5)[3:67])
names(raw_ESV_COIF230)[3:67] <- sub("^COIF230_", "", names(raw_ESV_COIF230)[3:67])
names(raw_ESV_COIF230)[3:67] <- sub("_PE$", "", names(raw_ESV_COIF230)[3:67])
names(raw_ESV_UNICOI)[3:67] <- sub("^UniCOI_", "", names(raw_ESV_UNICOI)[3:67])


#add column with what primer generated ESV
raw_ESV_BR5 <- raw_ESV_BR5 %>% mutate(primer = "BR5")
raw_ESV_COIF230 <- raw_ESV_COIF230 %>% mutate(primer = "COIF230")
raw_ESV_UNICOI <- raw_ESV_UNICOI %>% mutate(primer = "UNICOI")

```
